transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-11-05 15:00 PT | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Liam (CTO), Priya (Head of ML), Carlos (DevOps), Janelle (Product)

Summary (auto): QBR style review. Discussed rising token cost in September due to a spike in inference traffic, request routing/fallbacks, need for a Dedicated pool for predictable latency, and security docs. Action items assigned.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, with Ethan and Sofia — we'll run through the QBR then go into any technical bits.
00:12 Liam: Hey — thanks, Maya. Happy to be here. We got your invite. Quick note, got PTO overlap so Priya may need to step out briefly.
00:20 Maya: No problem. Agenda: usage/cost, reliability, security ask, roadmap and pilot.
00:35 Sofia: I'll call out the adoption metrics first — overall tokens up about 42% q/q mostly from chat prompts and higher average tokens per request.
00:48 Priya: Yeah that aligns, we shipped the new summarization flow in late August which increased context windows.
01:02 Ethan: On the reliability side, we saw two incidents in September — one degraded latency event during a region failover and a small rollout misconfig that caused longer tail latencies. We traced to prefix cache invalidation plus a fallback model spin-up.
01:20 Carlos: I pulled the incident tickets — the failover coincided with a K8s upgrade, a node spin-down in us-west-2. We had about 6 minutes of elevated p99.
01:35 Maya: Right — that aligns with our logs. There was a short burst where requests were routed to a smaller model variant for capacity reasons, which saved tokens but added latency.
01:49 Priya: That was visible in the product — we saw slower response for some end-users. We care about that p99.
02:02 Ethan: Quick technical note — the KV cache warm-up and the prefix caching behavior in Redwood Dedikated — excuse me, Redwood Dedicated — influences cold-start latency. For heavy prefix reuse you get a lot of benefit, but invalidations create the spike.
02:20 Janelle: Can you explain the commit/overage billing? We got a surprise credit in October but the September invoice was higher than expected.
02:35 Sofia: Sure — we send an invoice for hosted usage per-token. For Dedicated there's a reserved commit. The September spike was hosted usage because the flow used a larger base model more frequently. The credit you saw was a one-off usage rebate based on SLA.
02:52 Liam: Is moving to Dedicated the main lever to stabilize costs?
03:01 Maya: It's one of the levers. Dedicated gets you predictable throughput and a monthly commit, which usually lowers unit token cost for sustained workloads. Also, we can suggest quantization and batching profiles with Redwood Optimize to shave cost.
03:18 Priya: We're sensitive to latency also — Dedicated obviously helps but we need to know expected p50/p95/p99 for our peak qps.
03:31 Ethan: We'll run an end-to-end bench with your peak qps and the same prompt shapes — that'll give realistic 99th percentile numbers. We'll include KV cache warm-up scenarios.
03:44 Carlos: For the bench you need our peak qps number and the average request size, we can share that after this call.
03:52 Maya: Great — Carlos to send that as an action item.
03:58 (short cross talk)
04:10 Sofia: On security — Hawthorne asked about SOC2, SSO and KMS. We already have SOC2 Type II report, SAML SSO integration, and KMS options for Private deployments.
04:26 Liam: For audit purposes we want to export request-level audit logs monthly and get retention for 12 months in an external S3. Is that possible?
04:36 Ethan: Yes. We provide audit log export and an S3 sink for audit logs, and we can show how to set lifecycle rules. For Hosted we redact PII by default, for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and full logs.
04:50 Priya: Also, encryption at rest with customer KMS is a requirement for our compliance team.
04:57 Sofia: We'll share the KMS integration guide and the SOC2 packet.
05:05 Janelle: Any differences for on-prem/private vs Dedicated? We might explore Private later for data residency.
05:14 Maya: Private is a separate install and includes a customer-managed control plane and on-prem networking. Dedicated is still managed by Redwood but provides reserved GPU pools in our cloud. Private is heavier but gives the most control.
05:30 Liam: Good. For now we want to pilot Dedicated then evaluate Private if we need to meet data residency.
05:40 Ethan: Noted. We'll propose a pilot config: 2-4 GPU nodes, baseline batch sizes, and a warm-up plan for KV cache. We'll include an autoscale policy.
05:54 Priya: We also want to test rollback behaviors and canary rollouts — we had a minor rollout misconfig earlier.
06:03 Ethan: We'll include canary with gradual traffic shift and automatic fallback to the previous model variant; we can demo the policy in the pilot.
06:15 Maya: Pricing — I'll send committed capacity tiers and a sample SOW. We can propose a monthly commit that covers your baseline and a burst bucket.
06:27 Carlos: Bursting is important — some days we spike 3x baseline for a few hours.
06:34 Sofia: We'll document burst handling and queueing behavior — bursts are handled by reserved headroom or by fallback to lower-cost variants, depending on your policy.
06:50 Liam: Competitors — we've looked at Anthropic for chat quality and OpenAI for latency, but their managed pricing didn't fit our scale. We're also experimenting with Vertex AI for internal prototypes.
07:08 Maya: Good context. We'll include performance/cost tradeoff for the different variants and quantization options in the pricing doc.
07:18 Janelle: Dashboard and cost breakdown — can we get per-route token breakdown by model and by endpoint? That would help product owners.
07:28 Sofia: Yes — Redwood Console has per-route usage and token breakdowns, plus token-level cost. We'll share a sample dashboard link and a CSV export option.
07:42 Priya: For evals, we want regression alerts tied to a prompt set — can Redwood trigger alerts on percent change in pass rate?
07:52 Ethan: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports eval sets and regression alerts. We'll show sample alert thresholds during the pilot and include them in the runbook.
08:05 Maya: Okay, to recap: action items and next steps — I'll send pricing and SOW, Ethan runs the latency bench, Sofia sends SOC2/KMS docs, Carlos will share peak qps and request sizes, and we'll schedule a Dedicated pilot window starting around 2026-11-16.
08:25 Liam: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
08:30 Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot prep.
